Directions: Read the information in the box about the Dust Bowl on the Great Plains and look at the photograph. Then answer each question that follows.
Content:
:box:In `1862`, Congress passed the Homestead Act. Most of the settlers farmed their land or grazed cattle. The farmers plowed the prairie grasses and planted dry land wheat. As the demand for wheat products grew, cattle grazing was reduced, and `text(millions)` more `text(acres)` were plowed and planted. . . . Drought [began] in `1930`. . . . Winds whipped across the plains, raising billowing clouds of dust. The sky could darken for `text(days)`. . . . In some places, the dust drifted like snow, covering farm buildings and houses. `text(Nineteen)` states in the heartland of the United States became a vast dust bowl. With no chance of making a living, farm families abandoned their homes and land, fleeing westward to become migrant laborers.

	—Library of Congress
:ibox:Soil blown by Dust Bowl winds piled up in large drifts near Liberal, Kansas.
